plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the agent–environment interaction loop in reinforcement learning, depicted as a closed directed cycle between two rounded rectangular boxes filled with light teal. The upper box is labeled “Agent” with the policy π[a_t | s_t] inscribed inside, and the lower, larger box is labeled “Environment” with the state transition probability Pr(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) inscribed inside. Orange arrows with arrowheads form the loop: one arrow routes from the Agent box rightward and downward into the Environment box, carrying the action a_t; a second arrow returns from the Environment to the Agent carrying the current state s_t, while a third routes the next state s_{t+1} back around; additional arrow paths carry rewards r_t and r_{t+1}, and a label identifies the reward function Pr(r_{t+1} | s_t, a_t). Small white-background rectangles along the arrow paths isolate variable labels — State, Action, and Reward — for readability. This figure introduces the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework at the core of reinforcement learning, showing how the agent observes a state, selects an action according to its policy, and receives a reward and next state from the environment in a repeating closed loop.

interactionPlan.concept: Reinforcement learning is a closed loop: the environment hands the agent a state and reward, the agent's policy turns that state into an action, and the environment's transition and reward functions produce the next state and reward — one MDP time step.

Inside Agent box: 'Policy π[a_t|s_t]'
Lower, larger rounded rectangle, light teal fill with dark outline, title 'Environment'

Inside Environment box: 'Reward function' with 'Pr(r_{t+1}|s_t, a_t)'
Orange arrow: Agent → right side → down → into Environment right edge (action a_t)
Orange arrow: Environment right edge (lower) ← from far-right vertical path (reward channel routing)
Orange arrow: state path leaving Environment left edge at s_{t+1}, routing left and up into Agent left edge (labeled State s_t)
Orange arrow: reward path leaving Environment left edge at r_{t+1}, routing far left and up into Agent top-left edge (labeled Reward r_t)
Orange arrow: inner return path from Environment area up to Agent second input (State s_t)
Vertical dashed black line on the left of the Environment box representing the one-step time delay
Labels on the dashed line: 's_{t+1}' (upper) and 'r_{t+1}' (lower), each on a white background chip
Left-side outside labels on white chips: 'Reward r_t' and 'State s_t'
Right-side outside labels on white chips: 'State s_t' and 'Action a_t'
Arrowheads (orange, solid) at every path terminus

interactions.label: Play one MDP time step
interactions.teaches: The strict temporal order of a single RL time step: observe state and reward → choose action → environment responds with next state and reward, which become the next step's inputs.

Clicking the Agent highlights the policy π[a_t|s_t] and the outgoing action arrow (the agent's only output); clicking the Environment highlights the state-transition and reward-function distributions and their outgoing s_{t+1}/r_{t+1} arrows (the environment's only outputs).

interactions.label: Loop phase
interactions.teaches: Each phase of the loop can be visited deliberately, separating what the agent knows (s_t, r_t) from what the environment computes (s_{t+1}, r_{t+1}).

interactions.label: Show time delay (dashed line)
interactions.teaches: The dashed line is a one-step delay: the environment's outputs s_{t+1} and r_{t+1} are relabeled s_t and r_t when they arrive at the agent on the next tick.

demo_steps.title: The closed loop
demo_steps.narration: Two components only: an Agent holding a policy, and an Environment holding a state-transition and a reward distribution. Every orange arrow is information passing between them.

demo_steps.title: Agent observes s_t and r_t
demo_steps.narration: The environment's last outputs arrive at the agent as the current state s_t and reward r_t — these are the agent's only inputs.

demo_steps.title: Policy chooses a_t
demo_steps.narration: The policy π[a_t|s_t] maps the observed state to an action a_t, which travels around the right side into the environment.

demo_steps.title: Environment responds
demo_steps.narration: Given s_t and a_t, the environment samples the next state from Pr(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) and the reward from Pr(r_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) — both outputs depend only on the current state and action, which is the Markov property.

demo_steps.title: Time advances
demo_steps.narration: Crossing the dashed line, s_{t+1} and r_{t+1} become s_t and r_t for the next tick, and the identical cycle repeats forever.

demo_steps.title: Hide the delay
demo_steps.narration: Without the dashed delay line the diagram looks like simultaneous exchange — the delay is what makes it a sequential decision process rather than a single function evaluation.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The agent's only output is an action and the environment's only outputs are a next state and a reward — and because those outputs depend on nothing but the current state and action, the whole of reinforcement learning is this one Markov loop repeated.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two rounded rectangles on a white background, both filled light teal (#9ed8cd) with a dark charcoal outline and black serif/math text. The Agent box sits upper-center-right and is smaller; the Environment box sits lower-center and is taller, holding two stacked captions ('State transition' over Pr(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t), and 'Reward function' over Pr(r_{t+1}|s_t,a_t)). All connector paths are salmon/orange (#d9805c), orthogonal (right-angle elbows) with solid triangular arrowheads. Two paths enter the Agent's left edge (upper = Reward r_t from the far-left channel, lower = State s_t from an inner channel); two paths leave the Agent's right edge and descend the right side to enter the Environment's right edge (upper arrow = state routing, lower = action a_t). On the Environment's left edge, two short stubs exit toward a bold vertical dashed black line, tagged 's_{t+1}' above and 'r_{t+1}' below on white chips. Outside variable labels sit in the wide empty band between the boxes, on white chips so arrows appear broken behind them: 'Reward r_t' and 'State s_t' on the left, 'State s_t' and 'Action a_t' on the right. Highlighting should brighten the active path to a saturated orange with a thicker stroke and dim inactive paths to pale gray; box focus adds a glow/outline to the box and bolds its inner math.

discrepancies: Outer channel labels (Reward r_t, State s_t, State s_t, Action a_t) are rendered noticeably smaller relative to the boxes than in the source, where they are large display-sized text; likewise the dashed-line labels s_{t+1}/r_{t+1} are smaller and their subscripts are quite cramped.

The dashed time-delay line in the source is a heavy black line with long dashes and wide gaps; the generated version uses shorter, finer dashes, making it slightly less prominent as the 'time boundary' device.

Interior math strings in the Environment box (Pr(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t), Pr(r_{t+1}|s_t,a_t)) have very tight subscripts that read almost as inline glyphs, reducing legibility compared with the crisp LaTeX of the source.
Non-source additions: orange focus halos around boxes and yellow highlight chips on the delay labels appear during certain steps (acceptable interaction chrome, but not in the original).
evaluation.notes: Structurally an excellent near drop-in replica of the RL loop — correct box geometry, teal fills, orange routed arrows with correct arrowhead placement (none at the dashed boundary), and the dashed delay line — supported by genuinely pedagogical phase/step interactions; the only real weaknesses are undersized outer labels and cramped subscript typography.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items, verification is clean, and scores are near-max with only minor typographic nitpicks, so further iteration isn't warranted.
